$comment: GAP-HR-SF-09a role-matrix allowlist. Each entry is a KNOWN, currently-accepted drift between hr/layout.tsx's shared HR_ROLES (or a specific /hr, /hr/payroll or /hr/recruitment page's own tighter gate) and the backend route(s) it is responsible for -- discovered by scripts/contract/hr-role-matrix.mjs, a static analyzer that reads both sides live from source on every run. This file does NOT fix any of them (that is GAP-HR-SF-09b's job, gated on SF-20 and the relevant policy decisions per the campaign plan); it only lets the contract test pass today by naming each one, so the test can fail on a genuinely NEW, previously-unknown drift instead of on all 186 already-known ones every time. Never add an entry here to make a NEW drift disappear without asking why it exists first -- that defeats the point of the gate. `match` keys are matched against the analyzer's per-route report exactly: a route's (extraInBackend, extraInWeb, comparator) triple, both arrays compared as sets. GAP-HR-SF-09b (in progress) resolves these entry by entry -- see each removed entry's replacement commit for the resolution, and workRoles.ts's HR_ROLES doc comment for the biggest single cluster (GAP-HR-SF09A-001/002/003/011/012/014, resolved together by one widen).

driftEntries.reason: CONFIRMED INTENTIONAL by GAP-HR-SF-09b (no code change needed): hr_officer can open the disciplinary list/detail pages (DISCIPLINARY_ROLES admits it) but the 7 highest-stakes actions -- impose penalty, submit-approval, appeal-decision, close, drop, create suspension, revoke suspension -- narrow to hr_admin/super_admin only on the backend (hr_officer runs routine casework, hr_admin/super_admin signs off on the irreversible/severe steps). redesign/gaps/hr.md has no ROLEGATE (or any other) gap filed against this behavior, and services/hrms-service/tests/disciplinary-routes.test.ts ALREADY has an explicit, passing `it("returns 403 for hr_officer (needs hr_admin)", ...)` test for all 7 of these exact routes (penalty ~L513, submit-approval ~L575, appeal-decision ~L671, close ~L721, drop ~L780, suspension-create ~L835, suspension-revoke ~L940) -- the regression coverage this entry asked for already existed; GAP-HR-SF-09b just found and cited it. Left allowlisted because the drift is real and by design, not because it is unverified. 2026-10-07 (CI arch-contract lane, rebase onto current main): routeCount 7->8: one more disciplinary/routes.ts POST action landed on main with the same DISCIPLINARY_ROLES shape (hr_officer extra in web); same drift class, not a new mismatch.

recruitment/requisition-routes.ts admits a dedicated "hiring_manager" panel role that does not exist anywhere on the web side (not in HR_ROLES, not in any recruitment page gate). Plausibly by design -- ad hoc panel members likely reach requisition approval via a direct/emailed link rather than the general /hr nav -- but if that path doesn't exist yet, a hiring_manager-only account currently has zero way to use these 7 routes through the app.

ai-fraud/routes.ts (AI-assisted fraud detection alerts/scans/risk-scores/recommendations) admits audit_admin, which HR_ROLES doesn't have. Most likely intentional -- this is arguably an audit-service-adjacent surface hosted inside hrms-service -- but audit_admin has no way to reach it via /hr today.

gap-features/performance-dev-routes.ts (goals, development plans) admits a "dept_head" role absent from HR_ROLES and from every page gate. Same shape as GAP-HR-SF09A-005/009 (a participant role with no web-reachable path) -- listed separately since it's a different role name on a different file.

AMBIGUOUS, flagged for a product decision -- GAP-HR-SF-09b deliberately did not add this role. device-trust/routes.ts's block/unblock/policy-update endpoints admit it_admin, absent from HR_ROLES and every page gate, with no reference anywhere in apps/web. This module's device-trust dashboard route itself (GET /v1/hrms/devices/admin) has NO role check at all -- see GAP-HR-SF09A-019, deliberately out of GAP-HR-SF-09b's scope (a missing-guard security question, not a role-list drift) -- so this whole module's access story needs a combined security + product look, not a role-matrix side-fix. routeCount corrected 3->5 on 2026-10-01's rebase onto current main: device-trust/routes.ts grew two more it_admin-gated endpoints (now 5 call sites of the identical requireRole(["hr_admin","it_admin","super_admin"]) pattern at lines 203/255/286/303/329) since GAP-HR-SF-09b (this PR's first commit) wrote the reason above; same AMBIGUOUS/product-decision framing applies to all five. 2026-10-07 (CI arch-contract lane, rebase onto current main): routeCount 5->6: one more device-trust/routes.ts route now carries the same it_admin-only backend role as the other five.

AMBIGUOUS, flagged for a product decision -- GAP-HR-SF-09b deliberately did not add this role. recruitment/interview-scoring-routes.ts admits a dedicated "interviewer" panel role, same ad hoc-panel shape as GAP-HR-SF09A-005 (hiring_manager) and GAP-HR-SF09A-007 (dept_head). Note: apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/recruitment/[id]/page.tsx and InterviewCard.tsx DO reference "interviewer" -- but only as a display label/free-text id field (who a slot's interviewer is), never as an auth-role check; that page has no role-matrix-tracked gate of its own (not in scripts/contract/hr-role-matrix.mjs's PAGE_GATES) and relies on the layout default. Genuinely unclear whether an interviewer-role *account* is meant to use recruitment/[id] directly (vs. HR staff recording interviewer names on their behalf) -- needs a product decision, not a guess.

POST /v1/hrms/declarations/:declId/revoke (disciplinary/coi-routes.ts, Conflict-of-Interest declarations) admits a "vigilance_officer" role. This is UNRELATED to the /hr/vigilance page (that page covers a different backend concept, gap-features.ts's "vigilance cases", and its own VIGILANCE_ROLES cleanly matches gap-features.ts already -- see hr-role-matrix.json). "vigilance_officer" itself appears nowhere else in either service and has no web-side representation anywhere (not HR_ROLES, not any page gate, not even the /hr/vigilance page's own list) -- if this role is meant to have any web-facing capability, it currently has none at all.

Deliberate, intentional narrowing, not a bug: the published decision packet's own recommendation for GAP-HR-ICC-02 is "identity only through a dedicated icc_member-only detail route, audited -- the statutory default, not really optional." GET /v1/hrms/icc/complaints/:id is the ONLY route that ever returns complainantId/respondentId (POSH Act 2013 s.16) -- unlike the list route (GET /v1/hrms/icc/complaints, which correctly matches page:icc's ICC_ROLES: hr_admin/super_admin/icc_member), this detail route is icc_member-ONLY by design, excluding hr_admin/super_admin. A chairing hr_admin needs the icc_member role granted to them (a role-assignment decision, out of this fix's scope), not a code-level bypass on the one route that exposes identity. The analyzer maps this route to the page's shared ICC_ROLES comparator by file, not by exact path, so this drift is expected to persist until the analyzer grows a per-route-path comparator for icc-routes.ts's two GET routes.

CONFIRMED INTENTIONAL by GAP-HR-SF-09b (no source change needed): ADVANCE_ROLES admits manager/officer (and now also employee) to view and request salary advances, but PATCH .../approve and PATCH .../reject narrow to finance_admin/hr_admin/hr_officer/super_admin on the backend (loans-routes.ts HR_ROLES) -- an approval/rejection step correctly excluding the requester's own tier. Two regression tests in services/hrms-service/src/__tests__/loans-advances-manager-scope-real-db.test.ts ("GAP-HR-SF09A-015: manager ... cannot approve" / "... finance_admin ... can approve") lock the approve half of this in. Corrected on 2026-10-01's rebase onto current main: extraInWeb was [manager,officer] (routeCount 1, approve only) when GAP-HR-SF-09b first wrote this entry; employee was added to ADVANCE_ROLES by an unrelated already-merged change since then, and reject carries the identical backend role list to approve -- both now extraInWeb=[employee,manager,officer], routeCount 2. Caught only because this rebase re-ran the analyzer against current main, same as GAP-HR-SF-16/GAP-HR-SF09A-019's precedent. Left allowlisted because the drift is real and by design, not unverified.

NOT a real drift -- a confirmed analyzer false positive, found during the 2026-10-01 GAP-HR-SF-09b rebase. leave-policies/page.tsx imports LEAVE_POLICY_ADMIN_ROLES via the "@/lib/auth/workRoles" path alias; hr-role-matrix.mjs's getFileImports() only follows relative ("./", "../") import specifiers (`if (!spec.startsWith(".")) continue;`), so it never resolves this page's own gate, resolvePageConst() falls back to `{roles: null}`, and main()'s `comparatorRoles = resolved.roles ?? []` silently turns that into an EMPTY array instead of surfacing an error -- making every one of these 4 routes' real roles look like an unexplained mismatch. The real LEAVE_POLICY_ADMIN_ROLES (apps/web/src/lib/auth/workRoles.ts) is exactly ["hr_admin", "super_admin", "tenant_admin", "platform_admin"] -- an EXACT match with these 4 backend routes' own role list (leave/policy-admin-routes.ts's HR_ADMIN_ROLES), confirmed by direct source comparison, not assumed. Allowlisted as a known-false-positive rather than fixed here since the fix (path-alias resolution in getFileImports) is shared-tooling scope beyond this rebase; flagged separately as a follow-up rather than silently left unexplained.

NOT a real drift -- analyzer comparator false positive found 2026-10-07 (CI arch-contract lane, rebase onto current main): payroll-service payroll/routes.ts GET /v1/payroll/slips/mine (GAP-PAYROLL-SALARY-SLIPS-04) is the self-service My-payslips route and is deliberately employee-only (it returns only the caller own slips, resolved from the token). The analyzer maps it to the admin salary-slips page (SALARY_ADMIN_ROLES) by path prefix, so the roles look mismatched. Allowlisted as an analyzer comparator false positive; the real fix is excluding /slips/mine via OUT_OF_SCOPE_PATTERNS in hr-role-matrix.mjs, left as a follow-up.

noRoleCheckEntries.reason: Routes with no requireRole/requirePermissionKey call found at all -- any authenticated caller of ANY role reaches them (this is a materially different, more serious class of finding than a role-list drift, since it means the backend enforces no HR-role boundary whatsoever, not just a different one than the web expects). Sub-groups: (1) the "social" module -- kudos, kudos/feed, announcements, travel-requests, expenses(!), device registration, org chart, pulse-surveys, goals, leaderboard, AI assistant (19 routes across social/routes.ts + social/pulse-routes.ts). (2) gpf/routes.ts's four money-movement endpoints (subscription/advance/withdrawal/refund) -- no role check at all on PF transactions. (3) device-trust/routes.ts's admin dashboard, per-device activity log and policy GET routes (the /me ones are correctly excluded as self-service, see hr-role-matrix.mjs's OUT_OF_SCOPE_PATTERNS). (4) deputation/routes.ts's repatriate/cancel actions. (5) payroll-service's form16-verify POST route. GAP-HR-SF-09b (this PR) deliberately does NOT touch this bucket -- these are missing-guard security exposures, not role-list drifts, and fixing them means choosing what role SHOULD gate each one (a product/security decision), not reconciling two existing gates the way every driftEntries item above does; several (the money-movement gpf endpoints especially) deserve a dedicated security-flagged fix wave the same way GAP-HR-SF-16 got, not a role-matrix side-fix. routeCount corrected 32->30: GET /v1/hrms/social/feed and GET /v1/hrms/birthdays/today both now carry a real role check (confirmed via `git show HEAD:scripts/contract/hr-role-matrix.json` vs a live re-run) -- GAP-HR-SF-16 (self-scoping leak fix) landed on origin/main after this file's 2026-09-29 snapshot and evidently covered both in social/routes.ts's module-wide cleanup; unrelated to GAP-HR-SF-09b's own changes, caught only because this PR re-ran the analyzer against current main. None of the remaining 30 are fixed by this PR. routeCount further corrected 30->28 on 2026-10-01 (rebase onto current main, ~68 commits after this entry's prior 2026-09-29 correction): GET /v1/hrms/devices/admin and GET /v1/hrms/devices/:deviceId/activity (sub-group 3) now both carry a real role check (requireRole(ctx, ["hr_admin","it_admin","super_admin"])), landing alongside the two new it_admin routes GAP-HR-SF09A-008 now also tracks -- confirmed via `git show 4f135eaa9:scripts/contract/hr-role-matrix.json` vs a live re-run, same method used for the prior correction. Unrelated to GAP-HR-SF-09b's own changes. Remaining 28: device-trust's GET /v1/hrms/devices/policy and GET /v1/hrms/devices/me are still unguarded in that sub-group. 2026-10-07 (CI arch-contract lane, rebase onto current main): routeCount 28->38 (+10), all new on main since the 2026-10-01 count and none a missing-guard security exposure found by this lane: payroll tax-proofs/routes.ts GET :227 /mine and :285,:318 plus POST :367,:368 (employee-scoped via ownEmployeeTarget / role helper the analyzer cannot see), payroll fin03-routes.ts PATCH :316,:317 salary-revision approve/reject and pt-versions-routes.ts PATCH :101,:102 PT approve/reject (checks live inside the shared decide/decideRevision closures, not at the route call site), hrms scan-link-routes.ts GET :92 (internal service-to-service call gated by requireInternalServiceCall, not a user role). The role gates for the closure-based ones should be re-verified by a human reviewer; tracked here, not fixed in this CI lane. 2026-10-09 (PR #1939, GAP2-HR-SOCIAL-FEED-07): routeCount 38->36 -- POST /v1/hrms/kudos and GET /v1/hrms/kudos/feed in social/routes.ts now carry requireRole, so sub-group (1) shrinks from 19 to 17 routes. 2026-10-09 (fix/hr-staff-only-guards): routeCount 36->19. Closed by requireRole(ctx, STAFF_ROLES) (services/*/src/shared/roles.ts, excludes citizen/service_account): social/pulse-routes.ts pulse-surveys GET+respond, goals GET/POST/:id/checkin, leaderboard + my-points, assistant; social/routes.ts birthdays/:id/wish, travel-requests POST+GET, expenses POST, devices/register, orgchart; device-trust/routes.ts devices/heartbeat + devices/me; payroll form16-verify POST (+ per-user rate limit). That is 17 route registrations (the originating plan said 18; the enumerated list has 17 and this analyzer's tally dropped by exactly 17, 36->19). Of the remaining 19, 17 are guarded by a helper or inline check this analyzer cannot resolve to a role list, verified by reading each by hand and now annotated with a `guardedVia` field in hr-role-matrix.json: gpf subscription/advance/withdrawal/refund (post() helper -> requireRole(HR_ROLES)); deputation repatriate/cancel (close() -> requireRole(HR_ROLES)); salary-revisions approve/reject (decideRevision -> PAYROLL_ROLES + maker!=checker); PT version request approve/reject (decide -> PT_ADMIN_ROLES + maker!=checker); tax-proofs /mine (ownEmployeeTarget: employee + own id), list (requireViewer: payroll_officer/payroll_admin/auditor, no service accounts), :id/url (viewer or employee-owner, 404 otherwise), accept/reject (requireDecider + SELF_VERIFY_FORBIDDEN); scan-link lookup (requireInternalServiceCall: service_account + x-internal); expenses/:id/receipt (owner or EXPENSE_DECIDE_ROLES with reporting-line scope). The 2 genuinely unguarded left are read-only: GET /v1/hrms/devices/policy and GET /v1/hrms/announcements (tracked here, not in this change's scope).

dynamicEntries.reason: recruitment/offer-routes.ts's approve/return actions and recruitment/requisition-routes.ts's approve/return actions each call requireRole(ctx, [role, "super_admin"]) where `role` is a runtime-computed value (the specific approval-chain role for that requisition/offer's current stage), not a static list this analyzer -- or any purely static analyzer -- can resolve. Not a defect; recorded so the allowlist doesn't have to silently swallow "errors" on every future re-run, and so a human auditing approval-chain authorization knows to look at these 4 call sites directly rather than trusting this matrix for them. A 5th call site, service-book/pdf-routes.ts:39's requireRole(ctx, READER_ROLES), was added to this count on 2026-10-01 during a rebase onto current main -- but unlike the four above, its role list IS fully static (see this entry's full note in the rebase record); it only resolves as DYNAMIC because of a separate analyzer import-resolution bug (`.js` specifier vs the real `.ts` file), tracked as a follow-up rather than fixed in this change. 2026-10-07 (CI arch-contract lane, rebase onto current main): routeCount 5->12 (+7), all call requireRole with a role list built at runtime from in-file constants the analyzer cannot resolve: payroll fnf/routes.ts:367 (ACTION_GATE_ROLES[action]), tax-proofs/routes.ts:163,196,272 ([EMPLOYEE_ROLE]), :371 ([...HOLD_ROLES]), :382 ([...new Set([...VIEWER_ROLES,...RETENTION_ROLES])]), :406 ([...RETENTION_ROLES]). Every list is a static in-file const; not a defect. 2026-10-09 (fix/hr-staff-only-guards): routeCount 12->9. The analyzer now maps a `./x.js` import specifier to its x.ts source (the import-resolution bug noted above), so service-book/pdf-routes.ts:39 READER_ROLES and tax-proofs/routes.ts :371 ([...HOLD_ROLES]) and :406 ([...RETENTION_ROLES]) now resolve to static role lists and are classified MATCH, and the new `requireRole(ctx, STAFF_ROLES)` guards (imported from shared/roles.js) resolve too. No DRIFT count changed.

noBackendRouteFound.reason: No route in services/hrms-service or services/payroll-service serves this page (surveyed: all 783 routes across both services). "location_user"/"location_admin" do not appear anywhere in either service's role vocabulary. A sibling, non-hr-prefixed page (apps/web/src/app/(app)/locations/maps/page.tsx) and a large, wholly separate services/location-service (cadastral, geocoding, geofence, hierarchy, land-records, routing, etc.) exist in this repo -- location-service was NOT surveyed by this analyzer (out of the named scope: it is a general-purpose GIS platform service, not HR/payroll/recruitment-adjacent). Needs out-of-band verification: either hr/locations calls location-service under a path this analyzer wouldn't recognize as HR's, or this create form has no live backend at all. Excluded from the route-level allowlist above since there is no in-scope route to compare against.
